findings.title: New keyspace tests skip setup_tracing() unlike other new tests
findings.claim: keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill (:1474) and keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state (:1526) never call setup_tracing(), even though CONTRIBUTING.md says new tests should and the other new tests at :1869, :1945, :1973 do.

findings.title: Metrics fix commit adds decrement_total_connections with no test in same commit
findings.claim: Commit de164845 adds decrement_total_connections but its tests only arrive in the next commit 0d91aa54, violating CONTRIBUTING.md's requirement that bug fixes be covered with tests and each commit be coherent on its own.

findings.title: First keyspace test hand-builds PoolRefiller instead of reusing helper
findings.claim: The test at :1474-1496 constructs a PoolRefiller itself even though mock_pool_refiller() at :1754 does the same thing (duplicated code).

findings.title: Proxy rules duplicated from start_simulated_node instead of reused
findings.claim: The make_rules closure (:1529-1566) and proxy builder (:1580-1598) re-create the OPTIONS/STARTUP rules from start_simulated_node (:1809); the reshard test also hand-copies two more rule sets at :1877-1890 and :1904-1926 (duplicated code).

findings.title: New UseKeyspaceError message breaks the file's existing message pattern
findings.claim: The UseKeyspaceError variant's message doesn't match how the same variant reads elsewhere in the file (:79, :142, :172 use "'USE KEYSPACE <>' request failed: {0}"), and its neighbour variant uses transparent.

findings.title: Keyspace setup failure downgraded from warn! to debug! logging
findings.claim: A failure that now discards the connection is logged at debug! instead of warn!, making it quieter for operators than before.

findings.title: Commit message "Avoid busy-waiting" doesn't match what the commit does
findings.claim: Commit 617139df claims to avoid busy-waiting but only replaces yield_now() with sleep(1ms); the test at :2001 still polls the metric in a loop.

findings.title: Commit 7f48315d bundles three unrelated changes (Divergent Change)
findings.claim: The commit adds the fix, adds the new error variant, and moves the keyspace check ahead of maybe_reshard (:913-929), but the commit message doesn't mention the move.

findings.title: Failed USE never reverts current_keyspace, draining pool and marking live nodes…
findings.claim: PoolRefiller::use_keyspace stores current_keyspace before the USE is checked and never reverts it on failure (error propagates via cluster/worker.rs:767-797); after this PR, a nonexistent or dropped keyspace makes every refill connection fail (:900-911), draining the pool to Broken(UseKeyspaceError) and causing emit_events to send ConnectivityChangeEvent::Lost (:1175), marking up nodes as down even though the spec asked only to retry or drop the connection. The PR neither handles nor mentions this.

findings.title: A hung USE is neither retried nor dropped, stalling refills indefinitely
findings.claim: The TODO for a USE timeout is still present at :1336, so a hung USE keeps is_filling() true, stopping refills and preventing the Broken report at :908 from ever firing, even though the spec asked to retry or discard such connections; the pool-wide path (:1307-1313) does use connect_timeout but this path doesn't.

findings.title: Metrics balancing changes are out of scope for this PR/spec
findings.claim: Commits de164845, 0d91aa54 and 617139df fix total_connections when excess connections are cleared (:674, :1031) and on reshard (:1114), plus ~160 lines of tests; the logic looks correct but isn't part of the spec or PR description and belongs in its own PR.

findings.title: Sharder and port updates never applied while USE keeps failing
findings.claim: Because the keyspace check now runs before maybe_reshard, the shard-aware port update, and block_advanced_shard_awareness (:913-929), sharder and port changes are never applied while USE keeps failing.

findings.title: Keyspace failure logging at debug! makes pool draining invisible by default
findings.claim: The spec notes "the pool logs the error" but the log is now debug! (:903); combined with the pool-draining bug, a pool failing due to a bad keyspace makes no noise under default logging.
